rationale: Saloum's daughters join him in repairing Jerusalem, while the women in Exodus spin materials with their own hands for the Tent's work. Both expressly include women's labour in the community's building undertaking. The tasks and structures differ, and the daughters' particular skills or identities are not inferred from the spinners.
source_text: Next to him Saloum son of Alloes, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired, he and his daughters.

target_units.text: Every woman wise in heart spun with her hands and brought spun blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.
All the women whose hearts stirred them with skill spun the goats’ hair.

relationship: Shared named landmark in accounts of the city's rebuilding
rationale: Nehemiah locates priestly repairs above the Horse Gate. Jeremiah's description of a city to be built for the Lord includes the corner of the eastern Horse Gate in its sacred boundary. The named gate provides a particular geographical connection; the repair notice does not establish every boundary, the exact architecture, or the fulfilment of Jeremiah's promise of enduring preservation.
source_text: Above the Horse Gate the priests repaired, each opposite his house.

target_units.text: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and a city will be built for the Lord from Hanamel’s tower to the Corner Gate.
And its measurement will go out opposite them as far as Gareb’s hills, and it will be enclosed all around with chosen stones.
And all Asaremoth as far as the Kidron wadi, to the corner of the eastern Horse Gate, will be a sanctuary for the Lord. It will certainly never disappear or be torn down for ever.

relationship: Royal monetary demands borne by the land's people
rationale: The speakers borrow silver for the king's taxes, putting their property at stake. Joakim assesses the land so that its people provide silver and gold demanded by Pharaoh. Both show royal monetary demands falling upon the population and its resources. The rulers, assessments and occasions differ, and Kings does not say those payers borrowed or pledged their property.
source_text: Others said, “We borrowed silver for the king’s taxes—our fields, vineyards and houses are at stake.

target_units.text: Joakim gave the silver and gold to Pharaoh, but assessed the land to provide the silver at Pharaoh’s command. Each according to his assessment, they gave the silver and gold with the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Nechao.

relationship: A leader's account of restraint from personal gain
rationale: Within his account of governing Judah, the narrator says that he acquired no field. Samuel publicly asks whether he has taken anyone's animals or payments, and the people deny that he has taken anything from them. Both present restraint from personal gain as part of an account of public service; their declarations concern different assets, and the comparison is limited to these claims of restraint.
source_text: I did not take charge of the work on their wall; I acquired no field, and all those gathered there were for the work.

target_units.text: Here I am. Answer against me before the Lord and before His anointed: Whose calf have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Which of you have I tyrannized? Whom have I squeezed? From whose hand have I taken an appeasing payment and a sandal? Answer against me, and I will repay you.”
They said to Samuel, “You have not wronged us or tyrannized us or crushed us, and you have taken nothing from anyone’s hand.”
Samuel said to the people, “The Lord is witness among you, and His anointed is witness today, on this day, that you have found nothing in my hand.” They said, “Witness.”

relationship: Fear of God as a qualification for delegated authority
rationale: Anania, the ruler of the bira, is commended as truthful and fearing God more than many when the Jerusalem gate arrangements are entrusted to the officials. Jethro advises Moses to choose rulers who fear God, are righteous and hate arrogance. Both attach fear of God to delegated responsibility, while city security and judicial administration remain distinct and the differently worded additional virtues are preserved.
source_text: I gave orders to my brother Anania and to Anania, ruler of the bira in Jerusalem, for he was a truthful man and feared God more than many,

target_units.text: And choose for yourself from all the people able men who fear God, righteous men who hate arrogance; and you shall set them over the people as rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, and rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

And they shall judge the people at all times; the weighty matter they shall bring to you, but the lesser judgments they shall judge themselves; and they shall lighten your burden, and bear it with you.
